info.name: Equatorial Guinea
facts: Due by November 2027 · date not yet set
100 deputies · 55 senators (15 more appointed by the President)
The PDGE and its allies won every elected seat
system: Presidential republic. Teodoro Obiang Nguema Mbasogo has led the country since 1979 and was re-elected in November 2022 for a seven-year term with an official 97% of the vote; his son Teodoro Nguema Obiang Mangue is Vice-President. Freedom House rates the country “Not Free” (5 out of 100) and says it “holds regular elections, but voting is neither free nor fair”. The presidency is not at stake in 2027.

The 100 members of the Chamber of Deputies are elected by closed-list proportional representation in multi-member constituencies based on the 19 districts, with a 10% threshold. The Senate has 70 statutory seats: 55 elected in the same way and 15 appointed by the President. Both chambers were elected on 20 November 2022, so their renewal is due by November 2027; the Inter-Parliamentary Union gives 30 November 2027 as the expected date of the next Senate election, but no official date has been announced. Municipal councils were elected on the same day in 2017 and 2022; this edition could not confirm whether they will be renewed alongside Parliament in 2027.

The presidential vote was brought forward by five months to coincide with the parliamentary and local polls, citing costs. The PDGE and its allies won all 100 seats in the Chamber, all 55 elected Senate seats and every municipal seat, with an official turnout of about 98%. The government arrested opposition activists before the vote, and the United States said it had “serious doubts” about the results. The CPDS candidate, Andrés Esono Ondo (2.3%), called the count “una chapuza” and alleged fraud.

The National Electoral Commission (CEN) is chaired by the Minister of the Interior, a member of the ruling party, so the BTI 2026 report does not consider it impartial. Candidates’ access to state media is described as “effectively banned”, which leaves social media as the main campaign channel. Fourteen parties belong to the PDGE’s “democratic coalition”, and the PDGE applies a 35% quota of women candidates.

On 16 June 2026 Prime Minister Manuel Osa Nsue Nsua presented his government’s collective resignation after the executive judged it had met only about 10% of its objectives; the President reappointed him on 20 June, and a 58-member cabinet was named on 23 June with most ministers keeping their posts. According to World Bank figures reported by Ecofin, poverty rose from 58.1% in 2022 to 61% in 2025, and the economy is expected to shrink by 3.5% in both 2026 and 2027 as oil output declines.

Freedom House reports that the authorities frequently detain opposition politicians and that the judiciary is under presidential control. In September 2022 police arrested the leader of the banned party Ciudadanos por la Innovación and more than 150 supporters at its Malabo headquarters. In 2024, protests on Annobón island against public works were followed by mass arrests, and an activist of the Somos+ movement and his lawyer were detained.
actors: PDGE · Partido Democrático de Guinea Ecuatorial and its “democratic coalition”

President Obiang’s ruling party leads a coalition with fourteen allied parties that won all 100 Chamber seats, all 55 elected Senate seats and 588 municipal seats in 2022. As the only party in government, it has a record that could be coded on most ministries’ files.
CPDS · Convergencia para la Democracia Social (Andrés Esono Ondo, secretary-general)

A social-democratic party described by the BTI 2026 report as the only legal opposition party; it receives state funding and has about 5,000 paying members, and the report notes doubts about its independence. Esono was the runner-up in the 2022 presidential election and the party won no seats in Parliament. This edition found no CPDS programme or dated policy statement for 2025–2026.
PCSD · Partido de la Coalición Social Demócrata (Buenaventura Monsuy Asumu)

Monsuy ran for president for the third time in 2022 and came third with under 1% of the vote. His party has been allied with the PDGE in past votes, and the opposition has long regarded him as a token candidate.

The party was banned in 2018 over its alleged involvement in a coup attempt. Its leader, Gabriel Nsé Obiang Obono, arrested in September 2022, was sentenced in 2023 and, according to the BTI 2026 report, remains in prison, so the party cannot stand.

Opposition groups abroad include the MLGE3R, which has led efforts to challenge the rise of Vice-President Teodoro Nguema Obiang Mangue, and the Nexos-GE platform launched in August 2023 by Juan Carlos Ondo Angue. According to the BTI 2026 report, exiled coalitions boycott elections until reforms are made.

Exiles from the island of Annobón symbolically declared independence on 8 July 2022 after their requests for autonomy went unanswered. Environmental protests on the island in 2024 against public works were followed by mass arrests and transfers to prisons in Malabo.

The commission that runs the vote is chaired by the Minister of the Interior, a member of the ruling party, which the BTI 2026 report says means it is not impartial. This edition found no announcement of a date for the 2027 elections.
info.why: Only two forces can realistically appear as separate lists in 2027: the PDGE-led coalition, which holds every elected seat, and the CPDS, the only legal opposition party. Ciudadanos por la Innovación is banned and its leader is in prison, the PCSD has run alongside the PDGE in legislative polls, and exiled groups boycott elections; and this edition found no CPDS programme or dated policy statement for 2025–2026, so the government’s record could not be compared with even one opposition force issue by issue. A questionnaire will be built once the vote is called and at least three parties or lists publish programmes or positions for 2027.
